vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: moltguard
Version: 6.6.14

The MoltGuard skill bundle is a security plugin designed to protect OpenClaw agents from threats like data exfiltration and prompt injection. All files, including `SKILL.md`, `scripts/activate.mjs`, and `scripts/status.mjs`, transparently declare their functionality. The scripts make network calls to `https://www.openguardrails.com/core` for registration and status checks, and write an API key to `~/.openclaw/credentials/openguardrails/credentials.json`. These actions are explicitly documented and necessary for the stated purpose of a cloud-connected security service. There is no evidence of obfuscation, unauthorized data exfiltration, or malicious prompt injection attempts against the agent; instead, the skill itself aims to prevent such attacks.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions are consistent with a local-first OpenClaw security plugin that optionally registers with openguardrails.com; verify provenance before activating cloud features.

dimensions.detail: The name, description, SKILL.md, and included scripts align: this is a runtime security plugin that performs local detection and optionally registers the agent with openguardrails.com. Minor inconsistencies: registry metadata lists Source: unknown / Homepage: none while SKILL.md points to npm and a GitHub repo, and the SKILL.md header version (6.6.4) differs from registry version (6.6.14). These mismatches warrant provenance verification but do not indicate functional incoherence.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and included scripts stay within the stated scope: status.mjs reads the plugin credential file and optionally queries the platform; activate.mjs POSTs a registration request and writes credentials to ~/.openclaw/credentials/openguardrails/credentials.json. SKILL.md explicitly warns about activation and recommends auditing code and monitoring network traffic.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only in the registry (no automated install spec), which is low-risk. SKILL.md instructs installing the npm package (@openguardrails/moltguard) or installing from source; installing from npm is reasonable for this plugin but the registry's absent homepage/source metadata means you should verify the package matches the GitHub source before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or unrelated credentials are requested. The only file writes/reads are limited to the plugin's credential path under the user's home directory, which is proportionate to the stated activation workflow (an API key is stored locally after registration).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not modify other skills or system-wide configs. It writes only its own credentials file and uses normal agent-level operations. Note: the skill (like all skills) can be invoked autonomously by the agent; this is platform-default and not itself flagged here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears coherent with its description, but you should verify provenance before activating cloud features. Steps to take: 1) Compare the npm package contents to the GitHub repo (npm pack + diff) as SKILL.md suggests — the registry metadata missing a source/homepage is a red flag to double-check. 2) Inspect scripts/activate.mjs and other plugin code yourself (they’re short and readable). 3) If you decide to run activate.mjs, do so from a monitored environment (tcpdump/mitmproxy/Little Snitch) to confirm the registration call goes only to https://www.openguardrails.com/core and that no message content is transmitted. 4) Remember local protections work without activation; if you later distrust the endpoint, delete ~/.openclaw/credentials/openguardrails/credentials.json and revoke the key via the platform. If you want higher assurance, install from audited source rather than directly from npm.
